Anna (CS): Quick brainstorm: I want a compact customer-facing runbook for small/mid-market go-lives that covers caching, batching, streaming fallbacks, and a tiny feedback capture. Needs to be copy-pasteable into customer docs.

Mike (SRE): Agree. Keep it one page. I'll add two PromQL checks and a one-line recovery flow.

Sophia (PM): Recommend 4 parts: (1) instant readiness checks, (2) 2-step mitigation playbook, (3) pasteable SDK snippet, (4) feedback + renewal signal. Customers love explicit thresholds.

Anna (CS): Drafting now. Will make the language customer-friendly and also include an internal 'handoff' checklist for CS->SRE.

Raj (Customer): From our ops team: the #1 quick fix we do is bump cache TTL or temporarily drop streaming. Please include which to try first.

Mike (SRE): Short internal checklist for handoff: 
- Confirm model pinned (model id + commit)
- Check recent deploys in last 30m
- Verify cache warm (sample query below)
- Inspect 95th percentile latency for route in last 5m
If latency > target after config tweaks, escalate to infra lead.

ops-bot: Deploy event: customer/atlas-inc/prod v2026.03.11 at 1718459980 UTC.

Anna (CS): Customer-ready one-pager (copyable):

"Lite Onboarding: Fast Start Checklist"
1) Readiness (takes ~5 minutes)
  - Model & region: ensure model is pinned (ask your CS for the exact id).
  - Prefill cache: turn on prefix cache for repeated prompts (TTL=600s).
  - Batching: set target_batch_size=12 and max_latency_ms=120 to start.
  - Streaming: enable by default for interactive UX; disable temporarily if you see truncation or streaming stalls.

2) Quick mitigation (2-step)
  Step A (first 5 mins):
    - If 95p latency > 200ms or errors rise: increase cache TTL to 1200s and check cache_hit_rate.
    - If you rely on interleaved token streaming and see timeouts, toggle streaming=false for that route.
  Step B (next 10 mins if still degraded):
    - Reduce target_batch_size by ~40% (e.g., 12 -> 7) and set max_latency_ms=80.
    - If errors persist >1% for 5 minutes, switch to fallback_model=redwood-lite-v1 and notify your CS rep.

3) Telemetry to watch (first 30m):
  - 95th latency by route
  - error_rate (5m window)
  - cache_hit_rate
  - requests_per_minute (for surge detection)

4) SDK snippet (paste into onboarding config):
  {"model":"redwood-boost-1","prefill_cache":{"enabled":true,"ttl_seconds":600},"batching":{"target_batch_size":12,"max_latency_ms":120},"streaming":true}

5) One-line guidance: "Increase cache TTL when prompts are stable and reused; add prefill items when short, deterministic prompt fragments repeat at session start."

6) Feedback pulse (24h): send this short ask to your user ops team: "Any latency spikes, unexpected errors, or quality regressions? If yes, note route and sample input."

Anna (CS): Customer-facing escalation bullets:
- Tier 1: CS lead (Anna) 12h response for config suggestions
- Tier 2: SRE on-call (Mike) for latency/errors > thresholds after Tier 1 tweaks
- Tier 3: Infra lead for capacity or model fallback decisions

Raj (Customer): That flow is great. Can you add a tiny rule-of-thumb: when to prefer cache TTL vs adding prefill items?

Sophia (PM): One-liner suitable for customers: "Use higher TTL when the same prompts recur across sessions; add prefill entries when small, deterministic text (greetings, product IDs, short templates) appears right away in sessions and can be cached verbatim."

Mike (SRE): Prometheus / PromQL checks to include in the internal handoff doc:
- rate(redwood_infer_requests_total[5m]) by (route)
- histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_infer_response_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
- sum(rate(redwood_cache_hit_total[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_cache_lookup_total[5m]))
- sum(rate(redwood_infer_errors_total[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_infer_requests_total[5m]))

Anna (CS): Internal handoff note for CS->SRE (short):
- Paste the SDK snippet and current tenant config.
- Attach 24h feedback from customer and the 95p latency graphs.
- If flagged renewal_risk in CRM, mark high priority and include expected peak RPS.

Sophia (PM): CRM signal mapping: if customer answers 'No' to either latency OK or quality OK in the 24h survey, set renewal_risk=true and create a high-priority follow-up ticket.

Anna (CS): I'll assemble this into the onboarding kit and the one-page PDF. Thanks everyone! :sparkles: 

Mike (SRE): Added the PromQL checks to runbooks and created an internal quick playbook for heavy-throughput escalation.
